historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: The 5-year equity CAGR (12.3%) diverges by more than 30% from the 5-year revenue CAGR (9.2%) and the 5-year EPS CAGR (8.5%). Book value compounds faster than earnings because TTI pays out only about 48% of earnings and buys back very little. The equity CAGR is therefore not used as the growth selector, and EPS 5y is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - capex incl. capitalised development - lease principal + share-scheme purchases - SBC): FY2020 471.4, FY2022 72.4, FY2025 1,237.1. FCF CAGRs are dominated by the FY2021-22 inventory build and unwind (FY2021 owner FCF was deeply negative), so they are not a growth signal. The 3-year CAGR starts from the FY2022 trough. The owner-FCF 5-year CAGR (21.3%) is slightly ABOVE reported (20.7%). SBC has been falling as a share of revenue since FY2024 (0.40% to 0.26%), so stock compensation is not funding reported growth. Revenue growth slowed from about 9% (5-year) to about 5% (3-year) as the post-COVID DIY boom unwound. The forward base case sits between the two, at mid-single digits.

scenario_narratives.base: Milwaukee compounds in pro cordless, Ryobi grows mid-single digits on outdoor battery conversion, and the HART exit is a one-year drag. Group revenue grows 6.5-7% to 2028 and fades to 3.5% by year 10. Reported EBIT margin reaches about 10% one year after the 2027 internal target and holds about 10.5%. Owner FCF margin is about 8-9% after leases, SBC and Pillar Two cash tax.
scenario_narratives.bull: A US housing and R&R recovery combines with Milwaukee share gains outside North America to return growth to high-single digits. The rebalanced Vietnam/Mexico/US footprint and the post-IEEPA tariff relief let reported EBIT margin build toward 12%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Tariff costs out-run pricing at a concentrated retail channel (the largest customer, Home Depot, was 45% of FY2025 sales), and a weak housing cycle stalls demand in 2027. Margin reverts to the FY2023-25 ~8% EBIT level, growth runs about 3%, and the global minimum tax lifts cash tax to 16%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: TTI is valued as a high-quality cyclical durable-goods compounder on strict owner FCF. Lease cash, SBC and a rising cash tax are all charged in the flows, net cash is added once, and risk is carried in a bear-tilted scenario spread at a single USD WACC. The value is computed in USD and translated to HKD at the pegged rate, with ADR parity confirming the conversion.
key_risks_to_valuation: US tariff regime after the IEEPA strike-down (flat minimum tariff, possible Section 232 actions on tools)
Largest-customer concentration at 45% of sales (Home Depot; Ryobi and Ryobi-adjacent brands are Home Depot exclusives)
US housing turnover and repair-and-remodel cycle
Global minimum tax (Pillar Two) lifting a ~8% effective tax rate toward 15%
Capitalised-development write-offs (US$201m in FY2025) signal that R&D capitalisation flatters reported EBIT. The model charges the cash capex instead.
Working-capital swings: the FY2021 inventory build consumed US$1.7bn in one year

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (0669.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$83.20-150.00; ADR TTNDY used for the parity check
data_sources.financials: TTI Annual Reports FY2018-FY2025 and Interim Reports H1-2024/H1-2025/H1-2026 (research/0669.HK/Extracted), via 0669.HK_Metrics.csv; component lines read from the FY2025 cash flow statement and note 11, and from the H1-2026 interim EPS, share-capital and cash-flow notes
data_sources.qualitative: FY2025 annual report outlook and H1-2026 interim outlook (EBIT margin target 10% by 2027, FCF target raised to over US$1.3bn for 2026, HART exit, IEEPA tariff ruling)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, consolidated cash flow statement 'Share-based payments expense' US$39,310k (FY2024 US$58,811k). HK filer: no net-share-settlement tax withholding line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0). The company funds awards by buying shares on market for its share award scheme ('Net payment for purchase of shares for share award scheme', US$48,879k), and that payment sits INSIDE operating cash flow. To charge SBC once, reported_fcf adds that purchase back and the SBC expense is then deducted.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: weighted-average diluted shares for H1 2026, 1,832,535,767 (interim note on EPS). Shares in issue at 30 June 2026 were 1,828,237,441, after buying back 2.29m in H1 2026 and 3.5m in FY2025. The financial-parser's shares series (net profit / diluted EPS, about 1,832-1,840m) agrees with the printed diluted denominators to within 0.1%: FY2025 1,832.09m, FY2024 1,836.49m, FY2023 1,836.18m. The count is held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. Buybacks (US$41.7m in FY2025, US$34.5m in H1 2026) plus share-scheme purchases (US$48.9m) more than fund the flat count, so TTI is a repurchaser.
inputs.fx_note: The statements are in US$ thousands; HKEX 0669 is quoted in HKD. The model runs in USD, and per-share values are converted to HKD at USD/HKD 7.8472 (Yahoo USDHKD=X, 2026-10-10T21:00Z; HKD peg band 7.75-7.85). Parity check against the US ADR TTNDY (1 ADR = 5 ordinary shares): US$81.39 / 5 x 7.8472 = HK$127.74, against an observed HK$127.50. That is a 0.19% tie, which confirms the rate, its direction and the quote basis. The peg means FX drift is small, but refresh_price.py does not update this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The flows are USD, so WACC is built in USD: US 10-year about 4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta about 1.0-1.1 for a cyclical durable-goods maker, which gives cost of equity about 9.3-9.8%. The company is in a net-cash position, so WACC is about the cost of equity. Set at 9.0%, slightly below the CAPM midpoint, reflecting the #1 global pro cordless platform (Milwaukee) and 15 years of compounding. The same rate is used in every scenario: tariff, housing and execution risk sit in the scenario flows and the 20% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as an operating cost. The full lease cash payment is deducted through lease_cost_pct_path at 1.26% of revenue: FY2025 principal US$161.8m (financing) plus lease interest US$30.4m (inside interest paid), US$192.2m in total. Lease liabilities (US$149.0m current + US$602.0m non-current at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is bank borrowings plus discounted bills only. da_pct_path is D&A EXCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: amortization 221.2 + PPE depreciation 278.9, plus a normalized ~110 of the capitalised-development write-offs, about 4.0% of revenue), so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (US$0.1m or less in the equity statement). No NCI deduction is made and the flows are treated as attributable.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations: USD flows against an HKD quote, IFRS-16 leases, an SBC-light market. TTI is a standard operating company (cordless power tools, outdoor equipment and floorcare: Milwaukee, Ryobi, AEG, Hoover/Vax), so none of the bank, REIT, LIC or holdco rows apply. This is a first valuation with no prior memory entry. EBITDA BASIS: the ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC, pre-lease (IFRS-16) cash EBITDA = EBIT + all non-cash D&A including intangible write-offs + SBC. FY2025: 1,336.1 + 869.4 + 39.3 = 2,244.8, which is 14.7% of revenue. H1 2026 ran 15.4% on the same basis (1,260.5 + 20.5 over 8,291.6). Capex is PPE (288.96) plus capitalised development (300.90), 3.87% of revenue in FY2025. OWNER FCF FY2025 = OCF 1,979.2 - capex 589.9 - lease principal 161.8 + share-scheme purchases 48.9 = 1,276.4 (reported_fcf on this lease-consistent, pre-SBC-cash basis), less SBC 39.3, giving 1,237.1 (8.1% of revenue). INTEREST INCOME: TTI classifies 'Interest received' (US$63.0m) in INVESTING activities, so OCF - capex already excludes it. Stripping it again would double-strip, so interest_income is 0 here and net cash is added once in the bridge. Interest paid on borrowings (US$66.3m) sits inside the reported OCF, but the projection is built unlevered from EBITDA, so it does not enter the forward flows. NET CASH: cash 1,889.2 less bank borrowings and discounted bills 822.8 at 30 June 2026, giving net cash of 1,066.5. This is a mid-year balance and TTI's working capital is seasonal; FY2025 year-end net cash was 700.4. WORKING CAPITAL: about 15.5% of sales (inventory 106 days, receivables 46, payables 96), so a manufacturer's NEGATIVE capture applies: wc_capture -15% of the revenue increase. FY2021's -US$1.16bn FCF was a deliberate US$1.73bn inventory build, not a run-rate, and it makes the 3-year FCF CAGRs meaningless. GUIDANCE: FY2025 AR outlook: Milwaukee and Ryobi core up mid-to-high single digits in 2026, partly offset by the voluntary exit of HART. H1 2026 interim: revenue +5.9% and EBIT margin 9.9%; the internal target of 10.0% EBIT margin by 2027 is reaffirmed, with upside in 2028+; the FCF target is raised from over US$1.0bn to over US$1.3bn for 2026. The base year 1 (owner FCF of about US$1.33bn after lease principal) sits on that raised target. TARIFFS: the US Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20 and the administration followed with a flat minimum tariff. TTI's Vietnam/Mexico/US manufacturing rebalancing is the mitigation, and the outcome is carried in the scenario spread. BUYBACKS: TTI repurchases on market (US$41.7m FY2025, US$34.5m H1 2026), so the flat count is funded. HOUSE vs STREET: SBC is about 0.26% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow but not collapsed, and band_position is reported.

bear.narrative: The replacement US minimum tariff and any Section 232 actions raise landed cost faster than TTI can reprice through Home Depot (its largest customer, US$6.93bn or 45% of FY2025 sales, AR note on major customer), and a stalled US housing turnover depresses DIY and pro demand. Ryobi loses shelf space and price as Home Depot pushes alternatives, and Milwaukee faces Makita/DeWalt/Hilti price competition in a weaker pro cycle. Growth stalls in 2027, reported EBIT margin slips back to about 8% (the FY2023-25 level), and Pillar Two takes cash tax to 16%.

base.narrative: Milwaukee keeps taking share in pro cordless (M18/MX FUEL, trade-specific tools, and pipeline/power-utility categories) and grows high-single digits. Ryobi grows mid-single digits as petrol-to-battery conversion continues in outdoor. The HART exit drags 2026, so group growth runs 6.5-7% through 2028 and then fades to 3.5%. Reported EBIT margin reaches about 10% around 2028, one year behind the internal 2027 target, and holds about 10.5% thereafter. Cash tax ramps from about 8% toward 14% as Pillar Two minimum-tax regimes bite.

bull.narrative: A US housing and repair-and-remodel recovery as rates fall, combined with Milwaukee's share gains in new trades and international markets (Europe and APAC pro), takes group growth back to its 2015-2021 high-single-digit run rate. Operating leverage, the new Vietnam/Mexico/US manufacturing footprint and lower tariff costs after the IEEPA ruling lift reported EBIT margin toward 12% (the bull reading of 'further upside in 2028 and beyond').

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 20% from the 15% default. US tariff policy is still in flux after the IEEPA ruling, 75% of FY2025 sales went to North America (US$11.44bn of 15.26bn), and Home Depot concentration means a single-channel decision can move both price and volume. Base is held at 50%: the H1 2026 print (+5.9% revenue, 9.9% EBIT margin, FCF target raised to over US$1.3bn) is tracking it. Bull is trimmed to 30% because it needs a housing recovery and continued margin expansion together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: sanity_check.py historical_table() applies inputs.fx_rate backwards for every currency-mismatched ticker (documented bug, see memory sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug): it multiplies the already-HKD price by fx_rate instead of dividing by it to reach USD, inflating every printed historical and implied multiple by roughly fx_rate. Forced to false here rather than trust the scripts own true verdict, which was reached on garbage inputs. See sanity_check_note for the hand-bridged, correct-direction multiples.

sanity_check_note.reason: fx_rate direction bug in sanity_check.py historical_table() (quote HKD price multiplied by fx_rate instead of divided) -- same bug confirmed on 0288.HK, BA.L, and ~90 other currency-mismatched tickers.
sanity_check_note.basis: SBC-adjustment is negligible for TTI (SBC 0.26% of revenue), so these are close to GAAP multiples on both sides.
sanity_check_note.verdict: Both sit comfortably within the 10yr hand-bridged range -- a genuine pass, consistent with the DCF base case concluding the stock is close to fair value (-4.4% from the weighted IV). No driver changes made.
